summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic right knee pain due to mechanical loosening of a prior knee replacement underwent revision surgery to replace the tibial component. The procedure was performed without complications, and she tolerated it well. Postoperatively, she was managed with pain control, DVT prophylaxis with Lovenox, and physical therapy. Wound checks showed no signs of infection, and a staph swab was negative. Her hemoglobin improved from 8.5 to 9.4 g/dL during the stay. She was discharged to a rehab facility in stable condition with instructions for wound care, activity as tolerated, and follow-up in three weeks for staple removal. Discharge medications included oxycodone, acetaminophen, cephalexin, prednisone, metoprolol, albuterol, and enoxaparin for four weeks.
